semanticDecisions: Han Chang’an capital coordinates match the separately identified Han city area. Xian population rows are city-region references; they do not supply Tang palace or city boundaries.
Kyoto population records do not locate every Heian palace, temple or Nijō monument; the prose and context note distinguish the wider landscape.
Delhi Sultanate, Humayun’s Tomb and Shahjahanabad lie in different parts of the region. New Delhi 1911–1947 capital record is deliberately not bound to this medieval narrative.
Angkor record points are regional entry points; the population study point near Angkor Wat does not represent every successive Khmer capital.
Marakanda and Samarkand coordinates are not promoted to precise Afrosiab archaeological pins. UNESCO describes ancient Afrosiab and the later Timurid city as separate areas.
Baghdad source capital qualifiers begin in 763 while the new capital foundation is institutionally dated 762. These represent different claim types; neither source record is silently changed.
Humayun’s Tomb source contains 1560s in its detailed description and 1570 in its summary. The node uses circa 1570, not an asserted exact completion day.
Red Fort sources differ between 1638 and 1639 for construction start. The narrative node uses the consistently reported completion year 1648.

Pleiades Angkor description simplifies a 1431 abandonment. The narrative instead reflects the bounded Angkor Thom sediment research on gradual reduction of core activity; no date is used to erase all settlement.

APSARA currently has an inaccessible direct-page response for some pages, but complete institutional text was actually retrieved through indexed search results. That access mode is recorded; the guessed 2021/07/03/angkor-wat path is not cited.
A former UNESCO Silk Roads chapter link now redirects to the programme home page. The consulted UNESCO digital-library PDF and stable catalogue ARK are used instead.
